issues.title: fire_unit_until starts the firing with the blocking `mt-run minute`, so the trailing-phase stop never runs until the unit has already ended.
issues.why: fire_unit_until calls run(['mt-run', ...], stream=True) synchronously, and mt-run's start_and_stream loops `while is_running unit; sleep 2` before exiting. wait_for_unit_or_line only starts after the unit is inactive, so `reached and unit_active(unit)` can never be true and the stop never happens; the cutover waits for the whole unbounded pass. This is known bug B3, fixed later in f94c9e58.

issues.title: Judging per session makes any chunk with a genuinely empty session (no trades, halt) PARTIAL forever, so it is re-requested on every walk and never converges.
issues.why: judge_chunk_by_sessions returns PARTIAL whenever any closed session in the chunk has no bar in (open, close]. It cannot tell an unpublished session from one with no trades, so an illiquid or halted symbol's chunk stays open, increments attempt_count and is fetched again each cycle, spending quota. This is known bug B1, fixed in dc391881 with PROVIDER_HOLE and a publication-lag cutoff.

issues.title: The NOPASSWD root rule runs install-production.sh from the operator's own writable checkout, which makes it root-equivalent despite the header's 'limited root' claim.
issues.why: MT_INSTALL names /home/manta/source/repos/manta/trading-data/deploy/install-production.sh, in the manta account's own checkout, and grants it to manta as root with NOPASSWD. Anyone with that account's shell can edit the script and run it as root without a password. The header says the grant is limited, so this is a real security hole. It is not merge-blocking on its own, because the account already holds password sudo (preflight runs `sudo -v`), and the rule still points at the checkout at HEAD.

issues.title: The sudoers wildcards (`systemctl ... mt-*`, `mt-run *`) also match whitespace and extra arguments, so they cover other units and the whole production mt CLI as root.
issues.why: A sudoers `*` in arguments matches any characters, including spaces, so `systemctl stop mt-x sshd.service` or `start mt-x <any unit>` matches MT_UNITS. Under sudo, mt-run's fall-through runs run_production_mt, whose `-r env_file` branch execs the production mt binary as root with arbitrary arguments, though the scripts only need four fixed invocations. That is wider than the header's 'nothing wider', and 635fa500 later pinned the units and dropped the wildcards. sonnet-high/3/1 says mt-run runs as manta-trading, but root reads the env file and takes the exec-as-root branch.

issues.title: The sudoers rule does not cover the cutover's `sudo /opt/manta-trading/.venv/bin/python scripts/repair_921_minute_sessions.py` calls, so repair and verify still prompt for a password mid-run.
issues.why: _repair runs the production interpreter under sudo for --check, --apply and every --verify poll, and no alias in manta-ops matches it. After a long firing, or across the 15-minute verify polls, sudo prompts again. If the prompt times out, the output carries no FAIL text, and the cutover's substring verdict would then pass. The header's 'exactly the commands those scripts issue' is false. A later HEAD runs the repair unprivileged because 'root added nothing but a password prompt'.

issues.title: The new narration log tees only `say` lines, so the repair/verify output (the acceptance numbers) never reaches the log file.
issues.why: start_log only makes say() append to the file, and _repair emits the captured repair output with a plain print(). The [PASS]/[FAIL]/[WAIT] lines that start_log's docstring calls 'the cutover's report' are therefore absent from the file, while the closing message tells the reader to 'read the FAIL lines'. The new feature fails its stated purpose. It was fixed as review finding F002 in 635fa500 (log_text). It does not block a merge, because the terminal still shows the output.

issues.title: Acceptance is decided by the absence of 'FAIL'/'[WAIT]' text and ignores the exit code, so a crashed or refused verify counts as passing.
issues.why: The claim is true: `scan refused` on exit 2, or a traceback, contains no 'FAIL', and _repair only narrates the return code. But `ok = "FAIL" not in report` and the matching loop check were already in base. The diff only added the `[WAIT]` clause, and the defect (a missing verdict reads as a pass) is unchanged by it.

issues.title: Truncated days are passed to the seed only when seeding runs, and the frontier-only seed starts at MAX(gap_end), so truncated sessions behind a newer terminal row are never re-seeded.
issues.why: uncovered_days reaches compute_missing_minute_sessions only inside `if seed_from is not None`. With no UNKNOWN rows and a terminal row (for example a PROVIDER_HOLE or RETRY_EXHAUSTED for a recent session) newer than the truncated day, seed_from is the frontier, past the truncated day, or no seed runs at all. The truncation then stays silent, contrary to _build_truncated_index's docstring. The gating is unchanged at HEAD. How often that row state occurs in production is unverified, which is why confidence is low. It is not B2, which is the 7-day scan floor.

issues.title: The cagg freshness probe compares the refresh's finish time with bar created_at, so a refresh that started before the last bars were written reads as fresh.
issues.why: stale is `last_successful_finish < max(created_at)`, and created_at defaults to NOW() (transaction start), so bars committed during a refresh run can be missed while the probe says fresh. The race is real, but it can only undercount the session mass, which biases toward a spurious FAIL or one more poll and firing, never a false pass. The window is the refresh duration. This is low-value hardening rather than a merge blocker.

issues.title: The claim that the probe's `job.hypertable_name = <view name>` join matches no row, so verify would WAIT forever.
issues.why: For a cagg refresh policy, timescaledb_information.jobs.hypertable_name carries the view name. The existing cagg_freshness._JOB_SQL and cagg_repair use the same predicate, and cagg_freshness documents it. The lookup finds the job.

issues.title: The cagg freshness probe re-implements the existing refresh-job lookup and drops its '-infinity' normalization and scheduled/last_run_status signals.
issues.why: True duplication of cagg_freshness._read_refresh_job/_JOB_SQL. The missing nullif('-infinity') only matters for a policy that has never completed, which minute_4hour_ohlcv in production is not. A paused or failing job only makes verify WAIT for the bounded 5 polls and then report incomplete. That is a DRY point plus speculative hardening.

issues.title: The 04:05 UTC firing rationale assumes 20:00 ET = 00:00 UTC, which leaves only about five minutes of margin in standard time.
issues.why: The docstring's arithmetic holds only under EDT. In EST, 20:00 ET is 01:00 UTC, and the provider's 2-3 h upper bound is 04:00 UTC. The comment is wrong half the year and the margin is thin. A firing that misses publication only keeps the row and retries at 13:05, so the cost is a delay, not data loss.

issues.title: The mt-minute-pass.timer comment still says the minute pass is staggered 30 minutes behind the daily pass.
issues.why: The daily timer fires at 00:35/12:35, and the minute timer now fires at 04:05/13:05, so only the 13:05 firing is 30 minutes behind. This is a stale comment with no behavior impact. It was corrected in 635fa500.

issues.title: Import blocks added by the diff are out of isort order and fail the enabled ruff `I` rule.
issues.why: pyproject selects `I`, and ruff reports I001 on the new cutover_921 import block (line 45), which base did not have, and on minute.py, where new imports were placed out of order (that file and repair_921.py already failed I001 at base). This is lint and style only.

issues.title: The verdict markers '[WAIT]' and 'FAIL' are bare string literals matched across two scripts.
issues.why: '[WAIT]' is printed in the repair script and substring-matched three times in the cutover. That breaks the project's single-definition rule, but the code works as written today. It is a maintainability point.

issues.title: The new daemon tests copy-paste heavy mock scaffolding instead of reusing `_run`.
issues.why: Test-code duplication and log-string assertions in test_minute.py. These are test-quality points with no production behavior impact.

issues.title: The production daemon now imports the one-off slice-921 repair module.
issues.why: minute.py imports build_truncated_day_index and RepairScanTimeout from data/gaps/repair_921.py. That is true, but it is a module-placement and architecture point with no behavioral defect.

issues.title: fire_unit_until duplicates fire_unit's cursor/run/wait/sudo -v shape.
issues.why: The two functions share most of their body, and wait_for_unit_or_line repeats the poll loop. This is a DRY point. The blocking bug is graded separately as I1.

issues.title: An extra pool connection is opened per chunk for fetch_session_bounds while another connection is held, risking pool exhaustion.
issues.why: No other connection is held at that point. The seed connection is returned at line 792, the gap-pick chunk_conn is closed by line 833, and the write connection opens after bounds_conn closes. The checkouts are sequential, not nested, so the exhaustion or deadlock claim cannot happen.

issues.title: Each minute chunk now pays an extra connection checkout and session-bounds query.
issues.why: True: bounds_conn plus fetch_session_bounds run once per chunk. But each chunk already makes a 5-credit HTTP call and a write transaction, so one indexed query has no meaningful effect. The finding's side note about empty sessions exhausting retries is B1 (I2).

issues.title: Ctrl-C during a firing aborts the cutover script and releases the timers, despite the printed 'Ctrl-C only detaches, the script keeps waiting'.
issues.why: The Python process is in the foreground process group with no SIGINT handler, so Ctrl-C raises KeyboardInterrupt out of subprocess.run, and main()'s finally restarts the timers. The new fire_unit_until copies the misleading message from the pre-existing fire/fire_unit. The abort is visible to the operator and the running unit is unaffected, so the cost is a misleading message and a lost supervised run, not wrong data.

issues.title: The cutover loop fires another minute pass when verify is still WAIT after its polls.
issues.why: The loop breaks only on neither FAIL nor WAIT, so a WAIT that persists after the five 15-minute polls triggers another firing. With an hourly refresh, the 75-minute polling window spans a refresh, so a persistent WAIT needs an abnormal cagg state (a paused or failing policy). The point is true but limited to that edge.

issues.title: The narration log is created relative to the cwd before preflight checks the working directory.
issues.why: start_log(NOTES_DIR/...) runs before preflight(), and NOTES_DIR is relative, so running from the wrong directory leaves a stray notes directory and log before the CutoverError. That is harmless clutter.

issues.title: start_log truncates an existing file, and an OSError while writing the log would crash the cutover.
issues.why: write_text does truncate, but the file name is timestamped to the second, so no collision occurs in practice. An OSError while appending is speculative. This is hardening against inputs that do not arrive.
